title: Knap baby knap
content: The present administration’s focus on fossil fuels at the expense of emerging green technologies (https://doi.org/10.1093/biosci/biaf142) is a policy decision that is contrary to the ethos of the genus Homo, an ethos that likely dates back even earlier in our DNA to other hominid species. This ethos we are referring to is, of course, the embrace of new technologies and the omnipresent urge to improve on them. If you have not knapped a stone recently, then maybe the analogy might have been shunning anything to do with the combustion engine in favor of horse-based transportation. It is not good policy to refocus our quest for energy using older technologies by both subsidizing and deregulating the petroleum industry while doing the opposite for renewable wind and solar energy sources. Furthermore, the administration’s efforts to restrict research are contrary to the notion of human ingenuity where one person is—or, now, mostly a team of people are—internally driven to engaging or addressing a challenge in which they share a common passion.
